name: 境内个人 annual USD 50,000 convenience quota
summary: Buy FX at the bank with ID only, within USD 50,000 per person per year, then wire it out. The quota applies only to 境内个人 (PRC ID holders), so a US citizen is normally outside this route.
eligibility: Bank must classify the holder as 境内个人; quota is per person per calendar year; purchase purpose and payment purpose must match.
pros: Only an ID document is needed inside the quota
No SAFE approval
Published bank tariff and posted board rate allow a documented cost estimate
cons: USD 50,000 per year — USD 400,000 would need eight annual tranches under this model
A US citizen with a live PRC ID/hukou has a classification problem (see F02)
Splitting across other people's quotas is prohibited

steps.text: Confirm in writing how the bank classifies the account (境内个人 / 境外个人) and which ID is on file.
If 境内个人, present the valid ID and file the 个人购汇申请书 truthfully for a current-account purpose.
Buy USD within the annual USD 50,000 convenience tier; keep the purchase purpose and payment purpose consistent.
Wire the USD out; a single-day cumulative remittance above USD 50,000 needs transaction documents.
Pay the published BOC counter tariff (0.1%, min CNY 50, max CNY 260) plus CNY 150 international cable charge; overseas bank charges are passed through at actual cost.
Report the foreign account for the whole year it exists, including the year it is emptied.

name: 境内个人 above-quota current-account purchase with purpose documents
summary: SAFE states the USD 50,000 figure is a convenience tier, not a ceiling: a genuine current-account purchase above it is made with ID plus purpose documents.
eligibility: A real, documentable current-account use (tuition, medical, family support, etc.) and a matching payment purpose.
pros: No annual cap stated in the rule for a documented genuine current-account purchase
No SAFE approval
Avoids eight years of quota tranches
cons: Purpose evidence is required and bank-reviewed
Private study/travel/visiting-relatives FX is exempt from tax filing, but other service-trade payments above USD 50,000 need a tax filing
Fabricated purpose documents are a separate offence

steps.text: Identify the genuine current-account purpose and assemble contracts/invoices showing the transaction amount.
Choose the non-quota purchase channel at the bank; the 2026 SAFE Q&A confirms the taxpayer may elect not to consume the convenience quota.

Where the payment is a service-trade item above USD 50,000, complete the electronic tax filing and take the filing number/verification code to the bank; private study/travel/family-visit FX is exempt from that filing.
Buy USD and wire it out in one transaction; pay the published BOC counter tariff plus cable charge.
Keep the documents five years; report the foreign account in the US.

name: 境外个人 purchase against lawful China-source RMB income (Art. 59)
summary: For a US passport holder classified as 境外个人, Art. 59 permits purchase of FX against lawful current-account RMB income with ID plus source-of-funds materials including tax vouchers. No annual cap appears in the rule text.
eligibility: 境外个人 status; the CNY must be lawful, documentable China-source current-account income (salary, remuneration, etc.) with tax records.
pros: No annual ceiling appears in Art. 59 — the whole documented balance can in principle be converted
No capital-account approval
Matches the stated fact pattern best if the money is after-tax Chinese earnings
cons: Tax vouchers/source documents are mandatory — this is the 'considerable tax' the bank is actually asking about
Does not work for untraceable capital, property or inherited funds
Bank discretion over document sufficiency is not published

steps.text: Ask the bank to record the account subject category as 境外个人 against the US passport.
Obtain the official Chinese tax records / payment vouchers for the income that created the CNY balance.
Present ID, income/source evidence and tax vouchers; the bank buys FX for you (购汇) under Art. 59.
Wire the USD to your own US account; Art. 65 requires only ID for an 境外个人 current-account outward remittance from an FX account.
Pay the published BOC counter tariff plus cable charge; check whether an electronic-channel discount applies before using the counter baseline.
For US tax, express everything in USD at the prevailing rate; a personal FX gain up to USD 200 is not recognised under §988(e).

name: 境外个人 outward remittance of FX already held
summary: If the balance is already foreign exchange in an FX account, Art. 65(1) requires only the ID document for an 境外个人 to remit it out; no purchase, hence no conversion spread.
eligibility: Foreign currency already credited to the holder's FX savings account; the money is not currently CNY.
pros: No purchase step and no bid/ask spread
ID only under Art. 65(1)
Simplest documented bank procedure
cons: Does not help if the balance is CNY
Cash-form FX is limited to USD 10,000/day without a customs declaration or original withdrawal slip
Receiving/intermediary charges still apply

steps.text: Confirm the balance is 现汇 (account FX), not 现钞 (cash) and not CNY.
Present the valid passport/ID to the bank for an outward current-account remittance.
Wire to your own US account and pay the published BOC tariff plus cable charge.
File FBAR/8938 for the year; the account remains reportable until it is closed.

name: 境外个人 repatriation of unused inward FX / reconversion within 24 months
summary: Art. 14 permits an 境外个人 to remit unused inward FX back out; Art. 60 permits reconverting unused RMB from an original conversion with the original exchange memo within 24 months.
eligibility: Original inward remittance or original conversion memo; the 24-month reconversion validity applies to the memo route.
pros: Original path back out, with a clear document trail
Small same-day amounts (≤USD 500, or ≤USD 1,000 at departure) need only ID
cons: Requires the original paperwork
A second conversion incurs a second spread
Not usable for income earned in China

steps.text: Locate the original inward-remittance record or 原兑换水单.
For unused RMB, present ID and the original exchange memo within 24 months; the bank reconverts it.
Wire out under Art. 65 and pay the published tariff.

name: Current-account service payment with tax filing (e.g. tuition, medical, family support)
summary: Pay a genuine overseas current-account expense directly. A single external payment above USD 50,000 generally needs a tax filing (a reporting step), while private study/travel/family-visit FX is exempt from that filing.
eligibility: A real payee and a real invoiced service; not a disguised transfer of capital to oneself.
pros: Payment goes directly to the real expense, so no separate 'move savings' analysis
Tax filing is electronic and free; the 2021 supplement removed repeat filings for one contract
cons: This is spending, not moving a balance to your own account
Fake contracts/invoices constitute 逃汇/骗购外汇 exposure
Amount must match the underlying expense

steps.text: Collect the contract/invoice with the exact amount, payee and nature of the expense.
If the item is a single service-trade payment above USD 50,000 and not an exempt private-purpose payment, file the 备案表 online and keep the number/verification code.
Take the filing number (or the exemption position) and the transaction documents to the bank.
Buy FX and pay the overseas payee; pay the published BOC tariff plus cable charge.

name: 移民转移 — emigration property transfer
summary: The one general capital-account exit for a whole pre-emigration balance. The 2004 staged-release rule was cancelled in 2014; after approval, the bank may remit once or in instalments within the approved amount.
eligibility: A person who emigrated from mainland China (or to HK/Macao for settlement), applying at the former-hukou SAFE branch with hukou cancellation, a consular settlement certificate, property-title documents and tax clearance.
pros: The whole declared balance can be approved — not limited by the USD 50,000 convenience quota
2014 reform removed the three-year staging, the >CNY 500,000 head-office filing and notarisation
cons: Proof of legal source and tax clearance is mandatory — genuine tax may be due on the underlying income/gain
Requires emigration status documents a naturalised US citizen may not have
SAFE approval is discretionary; no published processing time or fee

steps.text: Confirm you meet the 移民 definition: property owned in mainland China before acquiring emigration status.

Apply once to the SAFE branch at the former hukou location with the written application, identity documents, hukou-cancellation proof, consular settlement certificate, property-title evidence and tax certificate/clearance.
Note that the 2014 circular cancels the staged-release requirement; the bank can remit once or in instalments inside the approved amount.
Take the approval letter and 核准件 to the FX bank; the bank must remit directly to your own account abroad, not pay out cash in China.
Pay the published BOC tariff plus cable charge; report the account in the US for the year.

name: 继承转移 — inheritance property transfer
summary: A foreign citizen who inherits mainland property may convert the estate and remit it after SAFE approval; different decedents no longer need separate applications.
eligibility: Foreign citizen / HK or Macao resident heir; inheritance, property-title and tax documents; application at the decedent's former-hukou SAFE branch.
pros: Whole inherited estate, not a USD 50,000 quota
2014 reform allows combined applications and single/instalment remittance
cons: Inheritance and tax paperwork is extensive
A US person receiving a foreign bequest above USD 100,000 must file Form 3520 Part IV
No published processing fee or timeline

steps.text: Gather inheritance proof, the decedent's property-title documents and the tax certificate/clearance from the tax authority.
Apply at the SAFE branch for the decedent's former hukou location; different decedents may be combined since 2014.
Take the approval and 核准件 to the bank for purchase and direct remittance abroad.
Check US reporting: a foreign bequest above USD 100,000 is reported on Form 3520 Part IV; it is generally not taxable income.

name: 境外个人 sale of mainland property, then purchase and remit proceeds
summary: Art. 22 of the individual FX measures allows an 境外个人 to purchase FX with the RMB proceeds of selling mainland property and remit it; the official Shanghai FAQ sets out the tax-voucher sequence.
eligibility: Property genuinely owned and sold; tax on the transfer settled; tax filing form required if the amount exceeds USD 50,000.
pros: Converts a large, specific asset balance in one documented path
No annual quota ceiling stated for this capital-account route
cons: 20% PRC IIT applies to income from transfer of assets — a real tax on the gain, not on the conversion
Requires the original purchase/tax records
US foreign tax credit may be relevant but is fact-specific

steps.text: Complete the property transfer and settle the tax on the transfer with the local tax authority; obtain the tax payment voucher.
If the outward amount exceeds USD 50,000, obtain the Tax Filing Form for External Payments for Trade in Services and Other Accounts.
Present passport, commodity-house transfer contract, registration certificate and tax documents at the bank.
Purchase FX and remit; pay the published BOC tariff plus cable charge.
Evaluate a US foreign tax credit for qualifying PRC income tax on the same income.

name: FIE dividend / profit repatriation (if the CNY came from dividends)
summary: If a foreign individual's balance came from dividends of a foreign-invested enterprise, a 2026 rule imposes 20% IIT and requires withholding; repatriation follows the documented-profit route.
eligibility: A foreign individual shareholder with FIE dividend income and tax records; the company must have withheld or the individual must self-remit.
pros: Documentable source of funds that supports an FX purchase
Treaty/credit analysis is possible
cons: The 1994 exemption was repealed effective 2026-09-01 — 20% IIT now applies
Not usable for a salary or savings balance
Corporate tax-filing steps are not published in the retrieved individual pages

steps.text: Determine whether the balance is FIE dividend income; from 2026-09-01 it is taxed at 20% as 利息、股息、红利所得.
Obtain the withholding/self-filing tax record from the company or tax authority.
Use the documented income to purchase FX at the bank under the individual FX rules; service-trade/repatriation tax filing may be required above USD 50,000.
Wire out and pay the published BOC tariff; evaluate a US foreign tax credit.

name: Wise CNY→USD (licensed partner, tax-record based)
summary: Wise's own pages allow non-mainland-Chinese individuals who work/worked in China and have China tax records to send CNY from their own account to their own overseas account. Single bank-app transfer cap CNY 300,000.
eligibility: Not a mainland Chinese national; current/former employment in China; valid Chinese tax record showing tax paid within the last three years; source account in the sender's own name; recipient account also in the sender's own name.
pros: Public quote shows the exact fee up front and a displayed mid-market rate
Fully online; no branch quota form
The 1% US remittance tax does not apply to a China-origin digital transfer
cons: Overall sending limit is tied to after-tax China salary evidenced by tax records — not a general capital exit
CNY 300,000 single-transfer cap from a bank app; larger balances need multiple transfers
Public quote pages above CNY 300,000 returned a waiting-list page on retrieval, so no quote was obtained

steps.text: Register, then complete the one-time verification (1-2 working days) with passport and Chinese tax records from the last three years.
Start a CNY→USD transfer to your own US account; the platform computes an overall limit from China salary and tax paid.
Pay by a domestic CNY bank transfer from your own account to the unique safeguarding account, or by Alipay; the CNY must come from your own account.
Wise converts at its displayed mid-market rate and pays out by local ACH/wire to the US; read the exact fee shown for your amount before confirming.
Keep the tax records; re-submit updated records when the overall limit is reached.

name: HSBC China outward telegraphic transfer (published tariff)
summary: The same lawful purchase/remittance steps through HSBC China, whose 2026 tariff publishes a different fee schedule: free for individual Private Banking customers; 0.1% (min CNY 100, max CNY 500) + CNY 120 cable for Premier/Advance.
eligibility: An HSBC China account at the relevant segment and a lawful documented purpose for the FX purchase.
pros: Published current tariff makes the bank-side cost verifiable
Private Banking individual customers pay no TT issuance or cable charge
'Pay Exact' option publishes a CNY 200 charge for full-amount credit
cons: Premier/Advance fees are higher than BOC's CNY 260 cap
The PDF embeds an older 2024 table — mixed vintage is flagged
Provider cannot override SAFE eligibility

steps.text: Confirm your HSBC China customer segment and the applicable tariff column.
Complete the same lawful FX purchase steps with ID and purpose/source documents.
Instruct the telegraphic transfer; the tariff publishes issuance, cable and optional Pay Exact charges.
Confirm whether overseas bank charges are borne by the remitter or deducted; the tariff states third-party charges are excluded.

name: Mainland-issued card spending abroad (no FX purchase)
summary: Use the CNY balance through a mainland card for overseas purchases. SAFE states its 2017 cash-withdrawal notice does not affect normal card consumption or the convenience quota; card consumption settlement is excluded from individual purchase/settlement reporting.
eligibility: A card linked to the CNY account and a merchant that accepts it.
pros: No quota consumption, no branch paperwork, no wire
Settles real USD-denominated expenses directly
cons: Not a way to obtain a USD balance — value is consumed, not moved
The card issuer/network conversion rate and fee were not published on the retrieved pages, so cost is blank
The CNY account remains FBAR-reportable

steps.text: Use the card for a genuine overseas purchase; the FX settlement is handled by the card scheme.
Check the card issuer's own rate/fee disclosure before a large purchase; no such rate was confirmed from an official retrieved tariff.
Continue reporting the CNY account in the US while it exists.

name: Overseas ATM cash withdrawal from a mainland card
summary: Withdraw cash abroad within CNY 100,000 per person per year and CNY 10,000 per card per day, paying BOC's published 12 CNY + 1% (max 112 CNY) per withdrawal.
eligibility: Mainland-issued debit card; the annual and daily SAFE limits apply across all cards of the person.
pros: Published tariff and published limits allow a bounded cost estimate
Does not consume the USD 50,000 purchase quota
cons: CNY 100,000/year cap makes a USD 400,000 balance a multi-year project
Cash in the US at USD 10,000 or more must be declared on FinCEN 105
A future tariff change effective 2026-11-11 alters Mastercard/Visa pricing

steps.text: Note the annual CNY 100,000 aggregate limit and CNY 10,000 per-card daily limit.
Withdraw at an overseas ATM; BOC charges 12 CNY + 1% of the withdrawal, capped at 112 CNY per withdrawal (tariff effective 2025-11-11).
From 2026-11-11, check the new notice: UnionPay pricing is unchanged, Mastercard/Visa becomes 2.5% with a USD 3 minimum and USD 40 maximum.
If carrying USD 10,000 or more into the US, file FinCEN 105 with CBP; declaring is free.

name: Physical cash carriage / hand-carried FX
summary: China limits outbound cash to CNY 20,000 or USD 5,000 equivalent without a permit; larger sums require a 携带外汇出境许可证. The US has no amount limit but requires a FinCEN 105 declaration at USD 10,000 or more.
eligibility: A permit for amounts above the Chinese limit, plus a truthful US declaration.
pros: No bank spread or wire fee
No tax on declaring currency in the US
cons: Undeclared currency risks seizure of the entire amount and criminal prosecution
Chinese-side permits and FX-cash purchase rates were not published in the retrieved tariff
Physically moving large amounts is the highest-risk option

steps.text: Do not exceed CNY 20,000 / USD 5,000 equivalent without a 携带外汇出境许可证; use the customs red channel and written declaration.
At USD 10,000 or more entering the US, complete FinCEN 105 and declare verbally and in writing to CBP.
Never split the amount to avoid a declaration; structuring is a separate offence.

name: Hold CNY in place and use it over time
summary: Leave the balance as CNY. PRC savings-deposit interest has been temporarily exempt since 2008-10-09, but a US citizen still reports worldwide income and the foreign account.
eligibility: No FX approval needed; any holder.
pros: Zero conversion and wire cost today
Avoids an FX decision at an unfavourable posted rate
cons: Exposure to CNY/USD exchange-rate movement remains
US worldwide-income, FBAR and Form 8938 obligations continue every year
Does not achieve the stated goal of getting USD out

steps.text: Confirm the product is an ordinary savings deposit; interest from 2008-10-09 is temporarily exempt from PRC IIT.
Report any US-taxable income in USD at the prevailing rate; a US citizen is taxed on worldwide income.
File FBAR (aggregate foreign accounts >USD 10,000) and check Form 8938 thresholds each year.

name: Convert CNY to USD inside China and keep it there
summary: Buy USD and hold it in a Chinese FX savings account. This removes CNY/USD exposure but does not move value out of China, and the account remains foreign for US reporting.
eligibility: A lawful FX purchase (quota or documented purpose) and an FX savings account.
pros: Locks in a USD denomination without an international wire
Future outward remittance of account FX requires only ID for an 境外个人
cons: One-way conversion spread is still incurred
No cable/receiving fee yet, but no money has left China
FBAR/8938 exposure continues

steps.text: Complete the lawful FX purchase (quota or documented purpose).
Credit the USD to an FX savings account; account FX settlement rules apply.
Continue US reporting; a later wire will incur the published tariff.

name: Phased annual-quota use across calendar years
summary: The same quota route as M01, explicitly treated as a multi-year schedule: the tranche count is derived from the published USD 50,000 annual convenience quota.
eligibility: 境内个人 classification for each year; a genuine current-account purpose each time.
pros: No purpose documents inside each year's quota
Predictable published bank-side cost per tranche
cons: USD 400,000 takes eight years under the quota alone
Repeated cable charges and repeated exposure to future rate changes
Not a solution for someone classified 境外个人

steps.text: Each calendar year, use at most USD 50,000 of the convenience quota with ID only.
Keep the purchase purpose and the wire purpose consistent each year.
Pay the published BOC tariff and cable charge for each tranche; re-check the tariff each year.
File US reports each year; consider the above-quota documented route (M02/M03) instead of waiting.

name: Splitting across relatives' / friends' quotas
summary: Art. 7 and Art. 62 prohibit 分拆 to evade quota/reality management; SAFE applies a 关注名单 for the year of listing plus two following years.
eligibility: Not available lawfully.
cons: Watch-listing and counter-level risk notices
All quota purchases then require full transaction documents for three years
May also be 逃汇 exposure under the Regulations

name: Underground banks / mirror swaps / private FX brokers
summary: Private or disguised FX trading is prohibited; Art. 45 sets a fine up to 30% of the amount, or 30%-100% if serious, plus confiscation and possible criminal referral.
eligibility: Not available lawfully.
cons: Confiscation of illegal gains
Fine up to 30% / 30%-100% of the amount
No legal recourse if the counterparty disappears

name: False trade invoices or fabricated service contracts
summary: Using false documents to purchase FX or move capital is 逃汇 / 骗购外汇 under Arts. 39-40, with a fine up to 30% or 30%-100% if serious.
eligibility: Not available lawfully.
cons: Fine up to 30% / 30%-100% of the amount
Order to repatriate or reverse the FX
Criminal referral

name: Crypto / stablecoin bridge
summary: PBOC Yinfa [2021] No.237 classifies fiat↔virtual-currency exchange and offshore exchange services to mainland residents as illegal financial activity, strictly prohibited.
eligibility: Not available lawfully.
cons: Prohibited outright
Financial institutions and payment providers may not service it
Civil-law transactions may be void; losses borne by the participant

name: Undeclared cash / structuring to avoid the US declaration
summary: CBP states unreported currency can be seized and may lead to criminal prosecution; 31 USC 5321(a)(2) allows an additional civil penalty up to the amount of the monetary instrument.
eligibility: Not available lawfully.
cons: Seizure of the entire amount
Global Entry revocation and criminal exposure
Structuring is a separate violation
